challenges.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
challenges.description: The order of vanishing of the L-function of an elliptic curve at s=1 equals the rank of the Mordell–Weil group.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify how τ-zeta or τ-L-functions interact with elliptic curve L-functions and rank conjectures.

challenges.title: Grand GRH and the Spectral-Arithmetic Hierarchy
challenges.short_title: Grand GRH and the Spectral-Arithmetic Hierarchy
challenges.description: How far does the τ spectral-arithmetic package extend beyond classical RH, and what external bridge conditions are needed for Grand GRH-style claims?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Specify the τ spectral-arithmetic hierarchy, distinguish what is internally addressed from what requires external bridges.

challenges.title: Hodge Conjecture
challenges.description: Hodge classes on a projective complex manifold are rational linear combinations of cohomology classes of algebraic cycles.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ's categorical / structural-position machinery applies to Hodge classes and algebraic cycles.

challenges.title: Langlands Program
challenges.description: A web of conjectured correspondences between Galois representations and automorphic forms unifying number theory, representation theory, and harmonic analysis.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State which Langlands correspondences τ can express, which it bridges, and where the framework adds nontrivial structure.

challenges.title: Navier–Stokes Existence and Smoothness
challenges.description: Establish or refute existence and smoothness of solutions to the 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify whether τ-dynamics imposes regularity, blow-up, or attractor constraints on Navier–Stokes-type evolution.

challenges.title: Poincaré Conjecture
challenges.description: Every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Recover or represent the relevant 3-manifold and Ricci-flow concepts within τ's structural grammar.

challenges.title: P versus NP
challenges.description: Are problems whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time also solvable in polynomial time?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ-address complexity or τ-resource grammar yields nontrivial complexity-theoretic constraints; do not claim resolution without registry-anchored evidence.

challenges.title: Riemann Hypothesis
challenges.description: All non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line Re(s)=1/2.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show how τ-zeta connects to or constrains classical zeta-function structure; clarify whether τ provides a new route, a re-description, or a structural analogue.

challenges.title: Yang–Mills Existence and Mass Gap
challenges.description: Establish a mathematically rigorous quantum Yang–Mills theory on R^4 with positive mass gap.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State whether τ provides nontrivial QFT-rigor route, mass-gap constraints, or only a re-statement.

challenges.title: Foundational Adequacy Challenge
challenges.description: Can a proposed foundation recover enough ordinary mathematics to support analysis, geometry, algebra, computation, probability, and mathematical physics without smuggling those structures in as hidden assumptions?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Classify all major mathematical structures as earned, imported, bridge-dependent, effective/readout-level, or not yet recovered. Make the no-hidden-runtime / no-hidden-substrate discipline auditable.

challenges.title: Linear / Resource-Sensitive Logic Challenge
challenges.description: Can mathematics be rebuilt or recovered with a logic that treats assumptions as resources rather than freely duplicable or discardable propositions?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State whether τ has a resource discipline. Identify whether contraction, weakening, duplication, deletion, and modal recovery of ordinary logic are earned or assumed.

challenges.title: Paraconsistent / Belnap-Style Logic Challenge
challenges.description: Can a foundation tolerate local inconsistency or incomplete information without trivial explosion, and if so, what formal logic governs that tolerance?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State whether paraconsistency is foundational, local, semantic, computational, interpretive, or not part of τ. If four-valued logic appears, specify the exact truth values, consequence relation, designated values, and relation to explosion.

challenges.title: Internal Logic Challenge
challenges.description: What logic is induced by the foundation itself, and how do classical, intuitionistic, modal, linear, paraconsistent, or many-valued fragments arise?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Identify the induced internal logic of τ and the conditions under which other logics appear as fragments, reflections, effective approximations, or bridge logics.

challenges.title: Set-Theoretic Strength Challenge
challenges.description: How much set theory does the framework recover, require, reinterpret, weaken, strengthen, or bypass?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain whether ZFC is recovered, interpreted, replaced, weakened, strengthened, or only used as ambient metatheory. Clarify the role of sets, classes, universes, replacement, power set, and choice.

challenges.title: Independence and Large-Cardinal Challenge
challenges.description: How does the framework handle mathematical independence phenomena and stronger axioms beyond ZFC, including large-cardinal-style strength hierarchies?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify whether τ produces analogues of large-cardinal strength, rejects them as non-τ-admissible, treats them as bridge artifacts, or reinterprets them as structural horizons.

challenges.title: Proof-Theoretic Strength Challenge
challenges.description: What is the proof-theoretic strength of τ or of its major fragments?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Give proof-theoretic comparison points: weaker than PA, comparable to arithmetic fragments, comparable to reverse-mathematical subsystems, comparable to ZFC fragments, or outside ordinary ladders.

challenges.title: Computability and Formalization Challenge
challenges.description: Can the foundation be represented in proof assistants without losing its intended semantics, and what exactly is checked by the formalization?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Specify what TauLib verifies, what it encodes, what remains prose-level, where bridge claims exceed formal proof, and how Lean's ambient foundations relate to τ's intended foundations.

challenges.title: Ontology of Mathematical Objects Challenge
challenges.description: What are mathematical objects: sets, structures, types, processes, constructions, positions, invariants, programs, forms, or something else?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State the τ ontology of mathematical objects and distinguish internal existence, construction, external interpretation, and physical legibility.

challenges.title: Pluralism versus Uniqueness Challenge
challenges.description: Is there one mathematical universe, many equally valid universes, or a structured hierarchy of internal worlds connected by bridges and invariants?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify whether τ claims unique foundational closure, controlled plurality, many internal worlds, or a terminal reflective structure that organizes plurality without erasing it.

challenges.title: Minimal Expressive Power Challenge
challenges.description: What is the minimum logical and axiomatic strength needed to recover the mathematics actually used in science?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Locate τ relative to known strength hierarchies where possible. Identify whether τ recovers scientific mathematics finitistically, constructively, predicatively, classically, impredicatively, or by a different structural route.

challenges.title: Finitism / Constructivism Boundary Challenge
challenges.description: How far can one go with finite, ultrafinite, constructive, or predicative resources before classical infinity, impredicativity, or stronger set-theoretic resources become unavoidable?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State exactly where τ sits on the ladder: ultrafinitary, finitistic, constructive, predicative, impredicative, classical, paraconsistent, categorical, type-theoretic, or sui generis.

challenges.title: Continuum Ontic-Status Challenge
challenges.description: What is the status of the continuum? Is it primitive, constructed, emergent, fictional, plural, effective, or bridge-dependent?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State whether the continuum is earned internally, appears as an effective/macroscopic object, is reconstructed from address limits, or enters only through a bridge.

challenges.title: Gödel Limitation Challenge
challenges.description: Does the system fall under Gödel incompleteness? If not, which hypothesis is changed?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Distinguish avoidance, relocation, controlled exposure, non-applicability, and ordinary vulnerability. Identify which τ fragments are effectively axiomatized and arithmetically strong enough for incompleteness.

challenges.title: Consistency and Relative-Consistency Challenge
challenges.description: Can the foundation give meaningful consistency evidence, or only relative consistency, model existence, proof-theoretic reduction, or local nontriviality?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Specify whether τ claims internal consistency, relative consistency, model existence, proof-theoretic reduction, paraconsistent nontriviality, or no global consistency claim.

challenges.title: Categoricity / Non-Categoricity Challenge
challenges.description: Can the intended mathematical universe be characterized uniquely, or does the foundation admit multiple non-equivalent models?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State whether τ is categorical, internally categorical, unique up to equivalence, model-plural, or model-relative.

challenges.title: Categorical Foundations Challenge
challenges.description: Can category-theoretic structure provide a genuine foundation of mathematics rather than only an organizing language over set-theoretic foundations?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ is merely category-flavored, category-theoretic in expression, or foundationally categorical in construction. Address size, universe, operation, collection, and unrestricted-category issues explicitly.

challenges.title: Type-Theoretic / Univalent Foundations Challenge
challenges.description: Can foundations be based on type, construction, identity, equivalence, and computation rather than membership and sethood?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain τ's relation to type theory and univalence: identity, equivalence, construction, proof-as-program, higher structure, and proof-assistant implementation.

challenges.title: Generic Hyperbolicity Challenge
challenges.description: Are one-dimensional dynamical systems generically hyperbolic, in the relevant smooth or complex-polynomial senses?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ supplies a notion of generic stabilization, attractor basin closure, or hyperbolic normal form that gives substantive constraints.

challenges.title: Algebraic Cycles and Limit-Cycle Challenge
challenges.description: For polynomial vector fields in the plane, can one bound or classify the number and arrangement of limit cycles as a function of polynomial degree?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ-cycle structure, address resolution, or basin decomposition gives a new route to bounding or classifying limit cycles.

challenges.title: Lorenz Attractor Recovery Checkpoint
challenges.description: Can τ recover, represent, or illuminate the structural role of chaotic attractors such as the Lorenz attractor?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show that τ can express the relevant attractor, stability, and verification concepts without claiming new external solution.

challenges.title: Local-to-Global Invertibility Challenge
challenges.description: If a polynomial map over a characteristic-zero field has constant nonzero Jacobian determinant, must it have a polynomial inverse?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ-holomorphic or address-theoretic structure can detect when local invertibility extends to global polynomial inverse structure.

challenges.title: Average Polynomial Solving Recovery Checkpoint
challenges.description: Can τ recover or compare with average-case polynomial-solving frameworks for systems of complex polynomial equations?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ-addressing and computational geometry can reproduce or explain the structural reason average-case polynomial solving becomes possible.

challenges.title: Formal Limits of Intelligence Challenge
challenges.description: What are the mathematical limits of intelligence, learning, and problem solving for humans and machines, and what formal model is adequate for such limits?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ can define intelligence structurally, distinguish symbolic/digital/analog/continuous computation where relevant, and articulate limits without abusing Gödel-style arguments.

challenges.title: Sparse Arithmetic Zero Challenge
challenges.description: Given a univariate integer polynomial described by a short arithmetic construction, can the number or structure of its integer zeros be bounded in terms of the arithmetic complexity of constructing the polynomial?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ supplies a genuine structural route to bounding integer zeros or only renames arithmetic-circuit complexity. Note: Smale's tau-conjecture is unrelated to Panta Rhei's τ except by notational coincidence.

challenges.title: Diophantine Addressability and Height-Bound Challenge
challenges.description: Can the existence of integer solutions to a two-variable Diophantine equation be decided within a uniform exponential-time bound, or otherwise constrained by a natural size/height measure?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ gives a notion of address window, height, or finite obstruction that yields nontrivial constraints on Diophantine solution search.

challenges.title: Central Configuration Finiteness Challenge
challenges.description: For arbitrary positive masses in the n-body problem, is the number of relative equilibria / central configurations finite?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ's dynamical or spectral structures impose finiteness, stability, or classification constraints on central configurations.

challenges.title: Spherical Capacity and Optimal Distribution Challenge
challenges.short_title: Spherical Capacity and Optimal Distribution Challenge
challenges.description: For N points on the 2-sphere, determine or algorithmically approximate configurations minimizing pairwise logarithmic energy.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ-capacity, boundary algebra, or spectral distribution yields nontrivial constraints on optimal point configurations or their asymptotic structure.

challenges.title: Strongly Polynomial Optimization Challenge
challenges.description: Does there exist a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for deciding or solving linear programming problems, independent of numerical bit-size in the relevant sense?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether τ-address geometry, interface width, or admissible transition structure gives a new invariant relevant to strong polynomiality.

challenges.title: What Is Life as a Structural Class?
challenges.short_title: What Is Life as a Structural Class?
challenges.description: Can life be defined as a structural class rather than as an empirical checklist of terrestrial organisms? A viable theory of life must distinguish living systems from nonliving systems, liminal cases, artificial systems, ecosystems, and nonterran candidates without relying only on Earth-biological examples.
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show that Life = Distinction + SelfDesc is not merely a slogan. The framework must demonstrate that the two predicates recover the classical hallmarks of life, generate useful phase boundaries, and make biological structure legible without reducing life to an arbitrary list.

challenges.title: Boundary and Individuality Challenge
challenges.description: What makes a living individual an individual? How are self/non-self boundaries established, maintained, repaired, and recognized across cells, organisms, colonies, ecosystems, immune systems, and artificial carriers?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show that τ-Distinction can represent membranes, organismal boundaries, immune recognition, ecological boundary ambiguity, and multi-scale individuality.

challenges.title: Life / Non-Life Phase Boundary Challenge
challenges.description: Where is the boundary between living and nonliving systems? How should viruses, spores, dormant cells, prions, autocatalytic chemical networks, AI systems, synthetic cells, ecosystems, and possible cosmic carriers be classified?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show which predicate fails or holds in each liminal case: Distinction, SelfDesc, metabolism, code closure, lineage, or repair. Avoid binary overreach where a graded or phase-boundary account is needed.

challenges.title: Metabolism, Energy Throughput, and Entropy Export Challenge
challenges.short_title: Metabolism, Energy Throughput, and Entropy Export Challenge
challenges.description: What is metabolism structurally? Why must living systems sustain energy throughput, maintain disequilibrium, and export entropy?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Recover metabolism as Life Loop Class rather than as a list of biochemical pathways. Show how energy circulation, proton gradients, ATP/ADP cycling, redox oscillators, and entropy export follow from the E₂ life structure.

challenges.title: Homeostasis, Repair, and Persistence Challenge
challenges.description: How do living systems maintain identity under perturbation? What is the structural relation among homeostasis, repair, persistence, and finite breakdown?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show how basin stability, repair budgets, self-maintenance, error correction, and defect accumulation arise from SelfDesc and Life Loop structure.

challenges.title: Ecosystems, Superorganisms, and Life-Basin Challenge
challenges.description: Are ecosystems merely collections of organisms, or can they form higher-order life-like structures? How should ecological coupling, population density, diversity, competition, mutualism, and collective behavior be understood structurally?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain ecosystem as multi-scale Life Basin or Poincaré circulation.

challenges.title: Agency, Cognition, and Decision-Making Challenge
challenges.description: How does agency arise in living systems? How do organisms sense, evaluate, decide, act, adapt, and coordinate behavior?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Recover agency as an E₂ sector, not merely a psychological property.

challenges.title: Neural Computation, Perception, Learning, and Memory Challenge
challenges.short_title: Neural Computation, Perception, Learning, and Memory Challenge
challenges.description: What is the structural basis of neural computation? How do perception, learning, memory, attention, neuroplasticity, and representation arise from living organization?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain neural architecture as τ³-computer or life-sector self-modeling substrate.

challenges.title: Consciousness, Language, and Life-Mind Bridge Challenge
challenges.short_title: Consciousness, Language, and Life-Mind Bridge Challenge
challenges.description: How is life related to consciousness, language, mind, machines, and culture? Which parts belong to E₂ structural biology and which parts require E₃ metaphysics or philosophy of mind?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State what is claimed at E₂: structural self-modeling, minimal conscious agent, neural architecture, language as shared code, life-mind bridge. Defer phenomenological content, qualia, and normative commitment to E₃.

challenges.title: Cosmic Life and Non-Organism Carriers Challenge
challenges.short_title: Cosmic Life and Non-Organism Carriers Challenge
challenges.description: Can the structural definition of life apply beyond organisms: to black holes, galaxies, cosmic basins, or other non-biological carriers? If so, what distinguishes a serious structural claim from metaphor?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show exactly how non-organism carriers satisfy Distinction and SelfDesc, whether they satisfy the seven hallmarks, and what empirical or formal consequences follow.

challenges.title: LUCA and Tree-of-Life Topology Challenge
challenges.description: What is the structural meaning of LUCA, and why does the tree of life have its observed broad topology? Is the bacterial/archaeal/eukaryotic split contingent or structurally expected?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify what is predicted: LUCA, three-domain topology, sectoral attractors, or broad regimes such as persistence, agency, source, closure, and consumer mixing.

challenges.title: Three-Domain Sector Taxonomy and Eukaryogenesis Challenge
challenges.short_title: Three-Domain Sector Taxonomy and Eukaryogenesis Challenge
challenges.description: Why do cellular life regimes include bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes? How should eukaryogenesis, endosymbiosis, organelles, mitochondria, chloroplasts, and the lipid divide be explained structurally?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show how the 4+1 Life sectors map to biological lineages without forcing arbitrary one-to-one correspondences.

challenges.title: Major Evolutionary Transitions and Multicellularity Challenge
challenges.short_title: Major Evolutionary Transitions and Multicellularity Challenge
challenges.description: Why do major evolutionary transitions occur: protocells, cells, eukaryotes, multicellularity, tissues, organs, social groups, and complex ecosystems?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Recover multicellularity as a colimit or integration of Life Loops; explain how cell, tissue, organ, organism, and ecosystem levels form without losing SelfDesc.

challenges.title: Open-Ended Evolution and Evolvability Challenge
challenges.description: What makes evolution open-ended? How do living systems continue to generate novelty, complexity, adaptation, and new regimes rather than exhausting a finite search space?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain evolution as PPAS or persistence-preserving adaptive search, and state what conditions allow open-ended novelty.

challenges.title: Origin and Maintenance of Sexual Reproduction Challenge
challenges.short_title: Origin and Maintenance of Sexual Reproduction Challenge
challenges.description: Why did sexual reproduction originate, and why is it maintained despite costs? What structural role does second distinction, recombination, or self/other coupling play in life?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain sex as second distinction or as a structural operation that expands search, repair, robustness, or SelfDesc variation.

challenges.title: Morphogenesis, Body Plans, and Organ-Size Control Challenge
challenges.short_title: Morphogenesis, Body Plans, and Organ-Size Control Challenge
challenges.description: How do living systems generate reliable form: tissues, organs, body plans, symmetry breaking, developmental axes, and correct size and shape?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain morphogenesis as projection from code/evaluator/time structure into spatial form.

challenges.title: Biological Time, Rhythms, and Developmental Timing Challenge
challenges.short_title: Biological Time, Rhythms, and Developmental Timing Challenge
challenges.description: Why do living systems keep time? How are circadian rhythms, cell cycles, sleep cycles, generation times, developmental timing, and seasonal rhythms structurally grounded?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain biological clocks as E₂ temporal structure rather than as unrelated molecular mechanisms.

challenges.title: Aging, Senescence, and Repair-Budget Challenge
challenges.description: Why does biological aging occur? Is senescence programmed, damage-accumulation-driven, repair-budget-limited, evolutionary, or structurally unavoidable for finite-lineage carriers?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain aging as monotone defect accumulation under finite repair budget; connect cellular, organismal, neural, and ecological scales.

challenges.title: Biological Homochirality Challenge
challenges.description: Why does terrestrial life use L-amino acids and D-sugars with near-universal handedness? Is homochirality contingent, environmentally selected, weak-interaction-seeded, or structurally necessary?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show how Kχ-coupled chemistry constrains chirality across all life-supporting regimes.

challenges.title: Universal Energy Currency and Chemiosmotic Coupling Challenge
challenges.short_title: Universal Energy Currency and Chemiosmotic Coupling Challenge
challenges.description: Why do living systems use energy currencies such as ATP/ADP and chemiosmotic gradients? Are these historical accidents or structurally constrained solutions for life-like energy circulation?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show why ATP/ADP-like oscillation, proton gradients, redox carriers, and enzyme stereospecificity arise from Life Loop structure and Kχ-coupled chemistry.

challenges.title: Origin and Structure of the Genetic Code Challenge
challenges.short_title: Origin and Structure of the Genetic Code Challenge
challenges.description: Why does the genetic code have its observed structure? How did codon-to-amino-acid mapping arise, and why does it exhibit degeneracy and error tolerance?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show whether the genetic code is derived, structurally constrained, or only re-described.

challenges.title: Central Dogma and Code-to-Form Morphism Challenge
challenges.short_title: Central Dogma and Code-to-Form Morphism Challenge
challenges.description: How does stored biological information become expressed form and function? What is the structural relation among genome, transcription, translation, proteins, epigenetics, and phenotype?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Recover DNA → RNA → protein as a morphism composition; explain mRNA as temporal bridge, tRNA/ribosome as adapter/decoder, and epigenetic state as evaluator context.

challenges.title: Folding and Sequence-to-Structure Challenge
challenges.description: How do linear biological sequences become functional three-dimensional structures? How should protein folding, RNA folding, allostery, and enzyme kinetics be understood structurally?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain folding as a categorical or geometric promotion from sequence to spatial structure, and clarify what τ contributes beyond existing computational biology and biophysics.

challenges.title: Protocell, Membrane, and Compartmentalization Challenge
challenges.description: Why does life require bounded compartments? How do membranes, protocells, organelles, and intracellular substructures arise and maintain distinct internal conditions?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Show how a membrane or boundary becomes a stable life-sector morphism rather than a passive container.

challenges.title: Abiogenesis as First Persistence Event
challenges.description: How can life arise from nonlife? What is the transition from prebiotic chemistry to a stable, self-maintaining, code-bearing, reproducing system?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explain the first emergence of a stable Distinction + SelfDesc carrier. The account must connect thermodynamic circulation, compartmentalization, code, heredity, and repair without assuming full biology at the start.

challenges.title: Structural Favorability versus Contingency of Life
challenges.short_title: Structural Favorability versus Contingency of Life
challenges.description: Is life structurally favored under the right physical conditions, or is it a rare accident of Earth history?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State what is meant by life is structurally favored. Distinguish necessity, high probability, basin attraction, weak inevitability, and mere compatibility.

challenges.title: Substrate Independence and Nonterran Life Challenge
challenges.short_title: Substrate Independence and Nonterran Life Challenge
challenges.description: Is life necessarily carbon-based, water-based, cell-based, and Earth-biochemical, or are there substrate-independent structural invariants of life?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Separate structural invariants from Earth-specific implementations. Identify which features are mandatory for life as such and which are contingent realizations.

challenges.title: Extraterrestrial Life and Biosignature Universality Challenge
challenges.short_title: Extraterrestrial Life and Biosignature Universality Challenge
challenges.description: If life exists beyond Earth, what should count as evidence? Are there universal biosignatures, or only Earth-biochemistry signatures?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: State which biosignatures follow from structural life: disequilibrium, boundary systems, energy cycling, chirality, code-bearing matter, atmospheric signatures, ecological feedback, temporal rhythms, or other markers.

challenges.title: Artificial and Synthetic Life Challenge
challenges.description: Can life be built, synthesized, simulated, or instantiated in non-natural media? What distinguishes a living artificial system from a simulation of life or a life-like machine?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Specify what an artificial carrier must satisfy: Distinction, SelfDesc, metabolism or energy throughput, autonomous repair, reproduction, heredity, evolution, and participation in a Life basin.

challenges.title: Truth, Truthmakers, and Coherence-Correspondence

challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through truth-bearers as sections, truth-makers as structures, sheaf condition, coherence-correspondence unification, Reg_D Proof.

challenges.title: Knowledge, Gettier, and Epistemic Luck

challenges.title: Qualia and Phenomenal Character

challenges.title: Cognition, AI, and Artificial Mind

challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through mind as internal topos, constructive consciousness criteria, minimal conscious agent, machine mind, dignity and commitment if applicable.

challenges.title: Perception and Cross-Modal Grounding (Molyneux Demoted)

challenges.tau_facing_burden: Treat Molyneux as a recovery checkpoint for cross-modal perception and unified consciousness rather than as a load-bearing E3 structural test.

challenges.title: Moral Knowledge, Moral Realism, and Normative Truth
challenges.short_title: Moral Knowledge, Moral Realism, and Normative Truth
challenges.description: Can moral claims be known, and if so, what kind of truth do they have?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through practical register Reg_P, commitment register Reg_C, dignity, CI operator, moral epistemology.

challenges.description: How can agents be morally assessed when outcomes, circumstances, or character partly depend on factors outside their control?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Coordinate agency, responsibility, commitment, moral register routing, narrative identity, external perturbation/stability.

challenges.title: Dignity, Normativity, and the Categorical Imperative
challenges.short_title: Dignity, Normativity, and the Categorical Imperative
challenges.description: Can dignity and categorical obligation be structurally grounded rather than merely asserted?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through dignity foundation, categorical imperative as fixed point/j-closed fixed point, practical and commitment registers, applied ethics.

challenges.short_title: God, Logos, Religion, and Ultimate Reality
challenges.description: How should the framework speak about God, Logos, religion, sacredness, and ultimate reality without confusing proof, metaphysical commitment, and personal stance?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Address existence of God, nature of God, epistemology of religion, science/religion boundary, Logos sector, no forced stance.

challenges.title: Proof, Commitment, and the No-Forced-Stance Boundary
challenges.short_title: Proof, Commitment, and the No-Forced-Stance Boundary
challenges.description: Where does proof end, and where does commitment begin? Can a formal framework recognize its own reflective boundary without collapsing into relativism or dogmatism?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through No Forced Stance theorem, commitment register Reg_C, proof register Reg_D, Logos boundary.

challenges.short_title: Being and the Question of Why There Is Something Rather Than Nothing

challenges.title: Ontic Adequacy and the Six Ontic Requirements
challenges.short_title: Ontic Adequacy and the Six Ontic Requirements
challenges.description: What makes a candidate reality admissible? Can a framework state necessary constraints on reality itself, rather than merely describe a model once reality is assumed?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Explicitly route through OR1 (self-coherence), OR2 (completeness), OR3 (generativity), OR4 (independence), OR5 (continuity), OR6 (stability).

challenges.title: Universals, Properties, and Structural Positions
challenges.description: Do properties, types, or universals exist independently, only in language, only in minds, or as structural positions within a coherent reality?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through Abstract Object as Structural Position and Non-Dualistic Platonism.

challenges.title: Objecthood, Individuation, and Boundary Conditions
challenges.description: What makes something one object rather than many, and how are boundaries between entities grounded?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through identity, address, boundary, and structural-position machinery.

challenges.title: Identity, Persistence, and Theseus-Class Transformations
challenges.description: When does an entity remain the same through replacement, transformation, repair, narrative revision, or phase change?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through three-level equality, identity slippage, address persistence.

challenges.title: Mathematical Objects and Abstract Reality
challenges.description: What is the ontic status of numbers, functions, categories, spaces, proofs, and formal structures?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Coordinate with the Mathematics SCL: abstract objects as structural positions, non-dualistic Platonism, proof codomain via Reg_D.

challenges.title: Realism, Anti-Realism, and Structural Realism
challenges.description: What does it mean for a theory to describe reality, rather than merely organize experience or language?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify whether τ is ontically realist, structurally realist, internal realist, register-relative, or commitment-relative.

challenges.title: Modality, Possibility, and Counterfactuals
challenges.description: What grounds statements about what could have happened, what must happen, or what would happen under altered conditions?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Route through modal logic, possible worlds as objects with accessibility morphisms, and counterfactual register routing.

challenges.title: Causation and Lawhood
challenges.description: What is causation, and what makes a law of nature more than a regularity, equation, or useful compression?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Bridge: Reg_E for empirical law, Reg_D for theorem structure, Reg_C where explanation becomes commitment.

challenges.title: Time, Temporality, and Persistence
challenges.description: What is the status of time: primitive, emergent, relational, internal to processes, or register-dependent?
challenges.tau_facing_burden: Clarify whether τ provides an account of temporal becoming or only of ordered states.
